function: Feed-forward DNN predicts transmit beamforming weights (communication and sensing, with nulls, side lobes, EIRP) at each UAV position; second DNN selects the associated ground BS (p. 9-10)
system: UAV with planar array (up to 100 patch elements) doing dual-function radar-communication to five ground BSs and one target; 0.3 THz, 100 MHz; no RIS (p. 4, 7, 8)
method: Two feed-forward DNNs: beamformer (50 hidden units) trained supervised on labels from a beam-pattern optimizer; association network (hidden 64, 32), label source not described; Adam (p. 2, 9-10)
data_channel: Own simulator: probabilistic LoS/NLoS air-to-ground path loss with THz absorption, 100 random UAV trajectories in a 1.5x1.5 km area; labels from a beam-pattern optimizer (p. 5, 7, 9)
test_conditions: Trained on 100 random UAV trajectories with a 70-30 train-test split; tested on held-out data and example trajectory points of the same area (p. 9-11)
baselines: Non-learned only: beam-pattern optimizer (time and patterns) and three association policies (closest GBS, minimum azimuth angle, highest SINR); no learned baseline (p. 10-11)
metrics: Beam-pattern error versus training epochs, SLL, EIRP, instantaneous communication rate, outage (SINR and EIRP), computation time (p. 9-12)
complexity: Measured time: optimizer 16 s per UAV position; beamformer NN 47 s training, 60 ms inference; association NN 20 s training, 30 ms inference (Table V, p. 10)
q1_support: p. 5: "we use a probabilistic path loss model, where the LoS and NLoS links are considered separately". Not met: custom THz air-to-ground model (free-space loss plus molecular absorption, p. 5); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "We have chosen a ratio of 70 − 30 for the training and test set." Not met: a held-out part of the same 100 random trajectories (p. 9) at 0.3 THz in one area; no new scenario, band or array configuration.
q3_support: p. 11: "comparing the three benchmark association policies defined and the proposed NN GBS association". Not met: these policies and the beam-pattern optimizer (Table V, p. 10) are non-learned; no earlier learned method or standard network is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "TABLE V: Computation time for the DNN proposed solutions": Beamforming Optimizer 16 sec, Beamformer NN 60 msec inference, Association NN 30 msec inference (measured runtimes).
q5_support: p. 9: "We have randomly generated NT = 100 different trajectories between the starting and final points." Not met: data come from the paper's own simulator and optimizer; no code or data link or DOI, and no public dataset.
notes: Preprint arXiv 2405.17015v1, submitted to IEEE TVT. Area 6 by the tie-break order (6 before 5): learned beam control of an aerial (UAV) link that also senses; area 5 is the alternative if the reviewer reads it as ISAC. The beamformer DNN imitates a classical beam-pattern optimizer (labels from it, p. 2), and its speed against that optimizer is the main claim. The association DNN acts above the physical layer but is learned jointly with the beams, so it passes the above-PHY check; the UAV trajectory is not learned (random trajectories). The abstract says ULA, the model uses a planar array (p. 4).
